newsitem.title: UK: Troubled gold price tumbles to three-year lows.
newsitem.headline: Troubled gold price tumbles to three-year lows.

text.p: Under selling pressure from all quarters and unwanted by fabricators and speculators alike, the price of gold slumped to three-year lows on Tuesday, and analysts said its prospects were unlikely to improve soon.
"In the short term, prices will slowly erode away, and rallies will be increasingly sold into. We're definitely heading south," said metals analyst Ted Arnold of Merrill Lynch.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see gold back at $330 in 1997."
Bullion fixed at $369.00 an ounce on Tuesday morning, the lowest fixing since November 1993, after slipping beneath the psychological $370 an ounce level overnight.

Prices have been declining steadily since a blistering rally pushed them to a peak of $418 an ounce in February. But over the past two weeks the descent has speeded up dramatically amid overwhelmingly bearish market sentiment.
Dealers and analysts have noted that mining houses, particularly in major gold producer Australia, have been in a panic to sell their output forward and lock in prices as the gold price sinks lower.
Persistent market talk that a central bank has been selling some of its gold reserves has also helped depress the mood.

"Institutions (like central banks) are not in the business of looking at price charts. If they have business they go ahead and do it, which makes it difficult for professionals to gauge the market," a London-based bullion dealer said.
Surging stock markets and a stronger dollar have also discouraged investors from buying gold and big investment funds are betting on the gold price sinking lower, analysts said.
Despite the plunge -- gold has shed some $15 since mid-November -- traditional buyers have held off to see how low prices will sink.
"There could be a slight recovery. But fundamentally I don't see anything that's going to push gold back up to the $380s," said market analyst Kevin Crisp of JP Morgan.
Over the next few months, physical buying was likely to emerge as jewellers restock after the winter buying season for Christmas, Chinese New Year and Ramadan, he said.
"... the real test for the market will be whether good physical demand is ignited by lower prices," Crisp added.
Underlying the bearish sentiment is concern in the market about gold's future role in European central banks, particularly in the rush to comply with European Monetary Union criteria.
If central banks decided to strip gold of its traditional role as the ultimate store of value and sell their reserves, the market fears it will be flooded with fresh, abundant supplies.
The other precious metals -- silver, platinum and palladium -- have followed gold. Silver, at $4.70 an ounce, is at 18-month lows and the other two white metals are at three-year lows.
